findings.issue: The page says admission 'applies the depth cap, the fan-out cap, the iteration budget, dedupe and cycle checks' and 'records a reason for each prune'. The code runs six ordered checks - relevance, dedupe, depth, fan-out, monotone budget, cycle - and prunes with the name of the first check that fails (frontier-admit.cjs:313-352). Two things are wrong: (a) the relevance check is missing entirely, yet it is the first one and prunes a proposal with no 'evidence', an empty 'scope', a scope outside the review target, or a parentId that is not in the store; it is its own prune reason, observed below as reason 'relevance'. (b) dedupe is checked second, before the depth and fan-out caps, so a duplicate proposal that also exceeds a cap is pruned as 'dedupe', not 'fanout' (observed below: the parent's cap is already full and the duplicate is still pruned 'dedupe'). 'the iteration budget' also mislabels that check: admission compares a child budget against its parent's (monotone narrowing), while the 50/35/15 iteration bands are applied by the reducer (reduce-state.cjs:2494-2533), not here.

evidence.cmd: mkdir -p $T/a; echo '{"maxIterations":10,"antiConvergence":{"depthMode":"expansive"},"expansiveDepth":{"maxDepth":3,"maxChildrenPerNode":1,"maxFrontierNodes":10}}' > $T/a/deep-research-config.json; frontier-admit.cjs seed --artifact-dir $T/a --iteration 0 --input $T/seed.json; frontier-admit.cjs admit --artifact-dir $T/a --iteration 1 --input $T/p.jsonl

fix.old: It applies the depth cap, the fan-out cap, the iteration budget, dedupe and cycle checks, and records a reason for each prune.
fix.new: It applies the relevance, dedupe, depth, fan-out, budget and cycle checks in that order, and records the name of the first failing check as the reason for each prune.

findings.issue: The page narrows the stop veto to 'a composite convergence stop'. For research the veto covers every stop candidate the run would otherwise take: both all_questions_answered and composite_converged are built with hardStop false, and the veto keys on '!candidate.hardStop', so either becomes CONTINUE/frontierOpen while a frontier node is open (convergence.cjs:1170-1173, 1190-1197). Only the cap, consecutive failures, stuck recovery, convergenceMode 'off', stopPolicy 'max-iterations' and the anti-convergence floor pre-empt it, exactly as the page's next sentence says. A run that is about to stop on all_questions_answered with open nodes is told the opposite here, and the overview in section 1 states the general rule ('holds a convergence stop'), so the page contradicts itself. The review loop is wider still - there the veto also holds the hard all_dimensions_clean candidate - which the review command doc states correctly.

The inbox row schema enumerates origin as 'one of angle-bank, analyst-strategy, operator, or legacy-import'. The research reducer's VALID_QUESTION_ORIGINS also accepts 'frontier', and that is the value frontier-admit.cjs writes on every inbox row an admitted frontier node queues (frontier-admit.cjs:409-415, origin: 'frontier', source: 'frontier'), i.e. the rows the --depth-mode=expansive frontier injects. An origin outside the set is normalised to 'operator' (reduce-state.cjs:207), so this list is the only statement of what the badge can read; it is one value short, and the value it omits is the one this run's own new mode produces. It also leaves the page's 'Question injection Surface' silent on the fact that a frontier admission on a research run appends to inbox.jsonl at all, which is why 'frontier' is missing.
